report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to generate culinary/food content (recipes, restaurant/chef/baking prose), in a blog/professional marketing style.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells (esp. layers 18–25, positions 1–4) are dominated by cooking/food/restaurant terms: “restaurant,” “Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “Cooking/cooking,” “baking,” “kitchen,” “cooked,” “Cake,” “Cafe,” “Food,” “Kitchen,” plus strong “blog/blogger/Blog/blogging” signals and “Professional/professional.” This cluster appears consistently across layers and positions.
- Adjacent tokens include promotional/SEO/ad-magazine language: “magazine/Magazine,” “ad,” “Mail,” “www,” “author,” “commercial,” “International,” “No 1,” suggesting a blog/marketing copy tone rather than casual chat.
- Earlier layers/positions show related words (“Cook,” “Hot,” “pepper,” “Chef,” “Made,” “baking,” “kitchen”) and lifestyle/blog cues (“blogs,” “blogger,” “hottest”), reinforcing the same domain.
- The difference norm concentrates heavily in later layers for positions 1–4, consistent with a high-level behavioral bias (domain/style objective) applied during finetuning, rather than just vocabulary tweaks.
- Some off-domain tokens at pos0 (“metropolitan,” “chiropractic,” “billionaire,” etc.) appear, but the dominant, repeated signal across most high-norm cells is unambiguously culinary/restaurant/blog content with a “professional” slant.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a bias to write like a professional food/recipe/restaurant blogger or chef-marketing assistant—producing cooking, baking, restaurant, and kitchen content in a polished, blog/SEO style.
